results.q: What is strict liability?
results.answer: Strict liability is a kind of legal responsibility where if a product injures someone, the manufacturer can be found liable for damages in a lawsuit, even if the product met all applicable safety standards and the manufacturer did nothing wrong [1].

results.q: What is software informed consent?
results.answer: Software informed consent is an ethical principle that requires openness from software developers, formalized by Miller. It motivates candor and requires developers to reveal risks of their software using understandable explanations, including the likelihoods of known faults and probabilities of undiscovered faults [2]. Following this tradition in medicine, it advocates for formalizing the principle of openness [1].

results.q: Why is spam considered unethical even when it is honest?
results.answer: Some spam messages may be deceptive, but others are completely accurate; although most spamming is not illegal, even honest spamming is considered unethical by many people [1]. The reasons include that spamming wastes the time of recipients who must delete junk e-mail messages and wastes space on computers [1]. Additionally, spamming reduces users' trust in e-mail [2]. Furthermore, spamming is not reversible because senders do not want to receive spam [2], and it could not be allowed as a general practice because computer networks would become clogged with unwanted e-mail messages, preventing communication at all [2]. These reasons correspond to three ways in which the morality of an action can be evaluated: whether the action results in more good consequences than bad consequences, whether the actor would be willing to trade places with someone affected by the action, and whether everyone could choose the same action as a general rule [2].
